**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 4(c), paragraph p0021**

The document's sole licence grant is the Section 4(c) licence to Contractor's Information incorporated into the Works. It is royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual and includes sublicensing rights — but:

- **Affiliates and contractors are not named** — the grant runs to "Company" only, and no defined term "Affiliate" exists anywhere in the agreement.
- **Not stated to be irrevocable** — perpetual alone leaves revocation arguments open.
- **Not transferable** — Section 10 (Nonassignability, p0042) bars assignment or transfer without the other party's consent, so there is no successor path on an M&A event.

Redline validated (ok:true) and finding submitted: a single minimal replacement in p0021 adding affiliates (with an inline control-based definition, since none exists) and contractors acting on our behalf, inserting "irrevocable", and making the licence transferable to a successor to our business or assets. The comment offers the fallback (affiliates on written notice; transfer limited to an M&A successor) if the Contractor pushes back.
